This Rpfc Is Filed Under Sec.19(4) Of The Family
Court Act, 1984, Against The Judgment And Order Dtd
08.01.2021 In Crl.Misc. No.76/2015, On The File Of The
Principal Judge, Family Court, Hubballi, Partly

 This Petition Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Present petition is filed by the petitioner/husband aggrieved by the order dated 08.01.2021 passed in Crl.Misc.No.76/2015 which was filed under Section 125 of Cr.P.C., by the respondents wife,
Basavaraj Alias Basavanneppa S/O. ... vs Jyoti D/O. Basavaraj Alias ... on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53750401/
2 daughter and son on the file of the Principal Judge, Family court, Hubballi (hereinafter referred to as the 'Family Court') in and by which the Family Court while allowing the petition directed the petitioner/husband herein to pay Rs.2,000/- each to the daughter and son per month till the date of handing over of their share in the family properties which are subject matter of the suit in O.S.No.78/2015 and further directed the petitioner herein to pay Rs.5,000/- per month as maintenance to his wife/respondent No.3.
It is this order which is questioned by the petitioner/husband.
2. Brief facts of the case are that the marriage of respondent No.3/wife was solemnized with the petitioner/husband on 26.01.2001 at Maruti Temple, Bhandiwad Village, Gadag Road, Hubballi Taluk.
That out of the said marriage, respondents No.1 and 2 being daughter and son were born.
That the respondent No.3/wife was subjected to physical and mental harassment at the hands of the petitioner/husband.
The respondent No.2/son is unable to speak as he needs the medical intervention for his tongue.

That upon the birth of the respondent No.2/son, the petitioner/husband left the matrimonial house and refused to take care of the respondents and deliberately failed to provide support in any manner whatsoever.
That the respondent/wife and children are staying separately.
It is also contended that the petitioner/husband is having landed properties and is having monthly income of about Rs.15 lakhs.
Despite the same, he failed and neglected to provide maintenance without any justifiable reasons.
That the respondent/wife and children had filed a suit in O.S.No.78/2015 and the same has been decreed.
Hence, sought for maintenance.
3. In response, the petitioner/husband appeared and contested the matter.

It is his contention that the respondents (wife and children) had filed a suit for partition in O.S.No.78/2015 and that a preliminary decree in the matter has been passed and as such there was no need and necessity for him to be directed to provide any maintenance.
As the respondents No.1 and 3 were self sufficient and respondent No.2 was given share in the property.

As regards the claim of the respondent No.3/wife is concerned, he contended that she has subjected him to harassment and has also filed unwarranted criminal complaints for the offence punishable under Section 498A and other sections of the IPC and that she was not entitled for any maintenance.

4. Considering the case of the parties, the Family Court by the impugned order partly allowed the petition directing the petitioner/husband to pay a sum of Rs.2,000/- each to the respondents No.1 and 2 (daughter and son) till their share in the properties subject matter of the suit in O.S.No.78/2015 was handed over to them and further to pay a sum of Rs.5,000/- to the respondent No.3/wife as maintenance.
5.

Sri. Vijay M.Malali, learned counsel for the petitioner/husband reiterating the grounds urged in the memorandum of petition, submits that the respondent No.1/daughter is already married and she is no more dependent on the petitioner or respondent No.3.
As regards the respondent No.2/son is concerned, a share in the property is already allotted and that is sufficient enough to provide financial and other support to him.
That the proceedings initiated by the respondent No.3/wife was not a bona fide one.
That she has deliberately parted the company of the petitioner/husband though he is always ready and willing to take her back.
That there is no justifiable reasons to stay away from the petitioner/husband, she is not entitled for any maintenance.

Hence, seeks for allowing the Basavaraj Alias Basavanneppa S/O. ... vs Jyoti D/O. Basavaraj Alias ... on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53750401/
3 petition and setting aside of the order passed by the Family court.
6.

sentences.text: Per contra, Sri. S.B.Doddagoudar, learned counsel for the respondents submits that there is no material evidence placed on record by the petitioner/husband to dispute the case of the respondents regarding they being in need of maintenance.
He submits that though a preliminary decree has been passed in the above suit in O.S.No.78/2015, the same is pending consideration in Final Decree Proceedings.
Till their share in the property is handed over to them and till the said property generates any income, it cannot be said that the said share is self sufficient.

He further submits that the respondent No.3/wife who was subjected to harassment at the hands of the petitioner was constrained to stay separately and was also constrained to have recourse to law by filing and initiating proceedings.
Mere initiation of the proceedings in accordance with law would not amount to harassment as they were necessary to protect her interest.
That does not absolve the petitioner/husband from providing maintenance to the wife.

7. Heard Sri. Vijay M.Malali, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. S.B.Doddagoudar, learned counsel for the respondents.
8.

The order of the Family Court directing the petitioner to pay a sum of Rs.2,000/- each to the respondents No.1 and 2 (daughter and son) till their share in the property is handed over to them is justified and does not warrant any interference.

Though it is contended that the respondent No.1/daughter is married and no more dependant, it is submitted at the bar that her marriage has taken place during 2021, while the petition for maintenance was filed in the year 2015.
The petitioner cannot be absolved of his liability to pay the maintenance from the date of petition till at least her marriage.
9. In view of this changed circumstance, the petitioner may avail such remedy in that regard as available in law.

10. As regard the order to pay maintenance to the respondents No.2 and 3 is concerned, the order of the Family Court does not suffer from any irregularity or any illegality in the facts and circumstances of the matter.
11. No grounds are made out.
12. Petition is dismissed confirming the order passed by the Family court.
13. Pending I.A.'s, if any, does not survive for consideration.
